text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The government is expected to discuss at its regular Tuesday session an amendment to the securities law aimed at bringing legislation closer to OECD standards.

- Parliament opens its May session on Tuesday with some 31 items on the preliminary agenda. The agenda includes the second reading of a draft law banning privatisation of the two largest commercial banks, VUB and IRB, proposed by the minor coalition party, the ultra-left Workers Party (ZRS).

- Parliamentary Chairman Ivan Gasparovic said he did not include discussion on the makeup of a parliamentary committee supervising activities of the secret service on the agenda because parties failed to agree on the number of members and the composition of the committee.

- The Constitutional Court said it would rule on the government request on whether the constitution can be changed by a referendum before the planned plebiscite on direct presidential elections later this month.

- The extreme-right Slovak National Party (SNS), a minor coalition party, said it would initiate a referendum on imposing the death penalty if the Constitutional Court rules that the constitution can be changed by a referendum.

- Roman Vavrik, parliamentary deputy of the opposition Democratic Union (DU), has taken Interior Minister Gustav Krajci to court for attemtps to thwart preparations of the upcoming referendum on direct presidential elections.

- VSZ, Slovakia's largest steel maker, said it expected the difference between production and market prices of rolled steel products to narrow in the near future due to increasing production in Europe.

- The banking sector will be short of liquidity of some four billion crowns on Tuesday ahead of the end of minimum reservers requirement period on Wednesday, which should push up the short-term rates on the interbank market.

SME - The ZRS and SNS, want to initiate parliamentary approval of a resolution asking the Russian Federation for a guarantee of support if Slovakia decides to become neutral. Chairman Ivan Gasparovic, a member of the senior coalition partner, HZDS, said he did not know about such an intention.

- Soccer's world governing body FIFA has approved a demand by the Czech Republic to postpone the World Cup qualification group six tie between Slovakia and the Czech Republic, originally scheduled for May 21. FIFA called for the two countries to open talks on the new date for the match.

- Investigation has not proved any crimes were committed in Slovakia by convicted Belgian child rapist Marc Dutroux, despite his numerous visits to the country before be was arrested for child abuse and murder last year.
- Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik on Monday returned from a four-day visit to China and Hong Kong where he held talks on economic cooperation.

PRAVDA - Eduard Kukan, parliamentary deputy of the opposition DU and former foreign minister, said excluding Slovakia from the first wave of NATO enlargement should not close the door for possible future membership. But Kukan said that NATO sould invite Slovakia in the first expansion round to maintain stability in the region.
